messages.author: be781b89be5de911
messages.subject: Installation problem
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to use RStan and follow the installation steps described in https://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/RStanGettingStarted
For the section C++ compiler, I have installed Rtools for my 64 bit window 7 platform. I follow the instruction to test whether my C++ compiler can be used by R, however I get the below error message. Do you have any idea why ? I can provide more information if necessary. 

> library(inline) 
> library(Rcpp)

Attaching package: ‘Rcpp’

The following object is masked from ‘package:inline’:

    registerPlugin

> src <- ' 
+   std::vector<std::string> s; 
+   s.push_back("hello");
+   s.push_back("world");
+   return Rcpp::wrap(s);
+ '
> hellofun <- cxxfunction(body = src, includes = '', plugin = 'Rcpp', verbose = FALSE)
Error in file(con, "r") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: running command 'C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-30~1.1/bin/x64/R CMD SHLIB file24f4614f37b.cpp 2> file24f4614f37b.cpp.err.txt' had status 1 
2: In file(con, "r") :
  cannot open file 'file24f4614f37b.cpp.err.txt': No such file or directory
> cat(hellofun(), '\n') 
Error in cat(hellofun(), "\n") : could not find function "hellofun"

Thank you,
Eric

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Installation problem
parts:
This isn't really a Stan problem at this point. My guess is that you have some sort of a write permissions problem (perhaps try starting R with administrative privileges) or maybe a problem with spaces in the file path (although I thought that was a thing of the past). Maybe someone reading this has experienced the same problem, but your best bet is probably to ask on the Rcpp list.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installation problem
parts:
On 7/31/13 8:48 AM, Eric Chan wrote:
> Hi Ben,
>
> Thank you very much for the help. I have tried to reinstall everything without the space and start R with the admin
> privileges. However, I experience the same problem. I have tried to post question to the Rcpp list and hope to get a
> reply soon. I have spent whole day working on it and want to use RStan as soon as possible.

I'm very sorry to hear that. Windows has given us no end
of problems on the development side, too, because the entire
open source C++ toolchain is so much weaker.

You definitely need to get Rcpp working before you can
install RStan. When it's sorted out, could you please post
back here with what the problem was and what needed to be done
to fix it? We're trying to build up the expertise to help more
people through Windows installs in the future.

For getting help from the Rcpp list, I'd suggest trying
to include more information on exactly what you did in terms
of installing and uninstalling applications. I don't know
enough about Windows to tell you how to do this exactly,
but your PATH will also be important. And as Ben said, this
looks like it may be a permissions issue, so there's the
matter of how you are logged in (as a regular user or admin),
which version of Windows you're using, which version of RTools,
what kind of shell you're using, and so on.

> Hope that someone who has
> experience this can give some hints on how to solve it.

I'm afraid that's not me. The only hint I saw online is that
it may have something to do with the R_HOME environment variable,
from Dirk's blog: http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2012/11/05/

I hope the Rcpp list or someone else here can help, but
as Ben says, you're currently hung up on installing Rcpp, which
is a pre-requisite for RStan.

- Bob

messages.author: be781b89be5de911
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Installation problem
parts:
Hi All,

Thank you very much for the support. After many hours of trial and error. I have my Rcpp installed successfully. 

Step 1. Uninstall everything 

(1) uninstalled R 2.15.3 and RTools30
(2) delete the folder of R and RTools 
(3) edit the Path within Environment variable to remove all RTools path

Step 2. Create another window account which doesn't have admin priviledge (Standard user). I use account with admin priviledge without success and try to use a standard user. Surprise that it work but don't know why. 

Step 3. Switch to the new user account and install everything

(1) Install R. I have unclicked the 32 bit version and click the 64 bit version instead. My installation path is  C:\R\R-2.15.3

(2) Install RTools using all the default setting. My installation path is C:\R\Rtools

Step 4. Create a batch file

(1) Create a file named Rgui.bat in the folder C:\R\R-2.15.3\bin\x64 with the below content

set Path=C:\R\Rtools\bin;C:\R\Rtools\gcc-4.6.3\bin
Rgui.exe

Step 5. Run the Rgui.bat and try to run the same code again. It is success.

I don't understand why it work. Anyway, I can proceed with my RStan installation now. 

Eric

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] OSes for dev team
parts:
I think there are a lot of things that are more important than Stan for choosing a new computer. But, at the moment, we don't do anything with virtual machines (although that shouldn't be a problem); there is one Windows desktop and various personal laptops with OSX and a few Linux. The Linux distribution shouldn't matter at all since we are relying on some of the most widely used C++ tools (g++ / clang++, Boost, and Eigen). I think most of the developers are using clang++ more than g++ themselves because clang++ compiles faster and uses a lot less RAM, but we wouldn't release a version of Stan that didn't work with g++ on Mac from XCode (actually llvm-g++) and Windows from Rtools (actually mingw-64).

Ben
